classification.difficultyReason: Justify approximately constant success probability for sampling without replacement and use the approximation.

content.prompt: A jury roll contains 2000 names, 700 of females and 1300 of males. Twelve jurors are randomly selected.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Explain why it is reasonable to make the approximation that the probability of selecting a male does not change with each selection.

answer.short: Only 12 of 2000 names are selected, so the male proportion changes very little.
answer.worked: Only 12 of 2000 names are removed, so the male proportion changes very little. It is reasonable to use $p=\frac{1300}{2000}=0.65$ for each selection.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Using this approximation, what is the probability of ending up with an all-male jury? Give your answer correct to 6 decimal places.

answer.worked:
Using $X\sim\operatorname{Bin}(12,0.65)$ for the number of male jurors,
$$\begin{aligned}P(X=12)&=\binom{12}{12}(0.65)^{12}(0.35)^0\\P(X=12)&=(0.65)^{12}\\P(X=12)&\approx0.005688.\end{aligned}$$
